question: Does it define a truly important problem?
Does it have a coherent model of users costs power and constraints?
Can it distinguish structural change from narrative hype?
Are product strategy and business model internally consistent?
Does the experience turn complexity into trust?
Can users quickly know what matters and what action to take?
Does the language create clarity rather than noise?
Does the product feel natural in repeated use?
Does it replace old workflows instead of adding a tool?
Does it move the cost curve meaningfully?
Does it redraw the boundary between product organization supply chain and infrastructure?
Can it create interfaces standards or ecosystem leverage?
Is it used in real production rather than demos?
Does usage convert into revenue margin or cash recovery?
Does usage improve the system through data or learning loops?
Does capital supply policy or procurement reinforce the system?
